current_workflow.step: In the evening, the desk lead writes a free-text email to the shift operators with the next day's long or short position: MW, hours ending, hub (NP-15 or SP-15), price, and the book the deals go under (ST-WBOM).
The same email covers other desks' positions (ST-CALI, St-SW), which have to be copied into the service sheet or looked up on Phil Platters sheet and in CAPS.

The lead, or Kate Symes, says which Enpower deals are already entered (by deal number) and which ones the shift still has to key or price in real time. Examples are purchases from the Calimbalance or the price on an EPE buy.
current_workflow.who: desk lead, deal entry (Kate Symes), shift operators

current_workflow.step: One-off duties go into the same email: APS losses, the hourly BPA check-out, NEVP transmission notice, unit ramp order and EES ancillary dispatch tracking in the Service Sheet.
When positions change after the first email, the lead sends a follow-up or forwarded correction, or corrects a standing instruction.
Shift operators report problems back by individual email. One example is dispatchers removing transmission requests that should have been withdrawn through the Pacificorp Oasis system.

implementation_steps: Draft the template from the recurring fields in the lead's last month of 'Length for' emails: hours ending, hub, MW, price, book, CAPS line, Enpower deal numbers, and deals still to key.
Add the template as a tab on the Service Sheet, next to the existing initials column for hourly BPA check-out calls.
Add the shift-end Return checklist and the standing-instructions log section to the same tab.
Agree with Kate Symes (deal entry) and the preschedule staff that they put Enpower deal numbers and tag status into the tab rather than in a separate email.
Run the template alongside the email for two weeks. The lead pastes the filled table into the DL-Portland Real Time Shift email so operators see the same layout.
Switch over: corrections become 'revised' rows, and operator problem reports, including dispatcher removals of Pacificorp Oasis requests, go only into the Return section.
After a month, review the Return sections with the lead and add any recurring item that still arrives by email.
risks: The evidence comes from one mailbox (williams-w3), and nearly all of it is the lead's sent mail. How operators actually report back is thinly evidenced, so check the Return section against the operators' practice before rollout.
If the lead goes back to free-text email under time pressure, the template drifts out of date. Mitigate by making the template the only place deal numbers and corrections are recorded.
The ST-CALI desk's own sheet may disagree with the handoff tab. Link to it rather than copying, and note the time of the last update.
The dollar value is small (about $52 a month). The case rests on fewer missed entries and contested charges, which this evidence does not quantify.

solution.approach: Replace the free-text evening email with a fixed shift handoff template, kept as a tab on the Service Sheet. A copy is pasted into the email to DL-Portland Real Time Shift. The desk lead fills one row per position: date, hours ending, hub, MW, long or short, price, book (ST-WBOM, ST-CALI, St-SW), the CAPS line, Enpower deal numbers already entered, and what the shift must still key or price. The other sections are fixed. 'Other desks' positions' links to the ST-CALI sheet rather than retyping it. 'Special duties this shift' covers losses, BPA check-out, NEVP notice and ancillary dispatch. 'Standing instructions changed' covers items like unit ramp order. Operators fill a 'Return' section at shift end: missed or changed schedules, transmission requests withdrawn or removed by dispatchers, and Enpower items still open. That gives the lead one place to read problems back. A correction is a new row marked 'revised' in the same tab, not a separate 'one more time' email.
components: shift handoff template tab (position table plus fixed sections)
shift-end Return checklist (missed schedules, Oasis withdrawals, dispatcher removals, open Enpower items)
'revised' row convention that replaces correction emails
standing-instructions log section (ramp order, BPA check-out, NEVP notice lead time)
inputs: next-day length and shorts by hour ending, hub and price
tags and preschedule entries made by preschedule staff
outputs: filled handoff tab on the Service Sheet for the shift operators
handoff email to DL-Portland Real Time Shift in the fixed layout
shift-end Return section for the desk lead listing missed schedules, open Enpower items and transmission removals
solution.trigger: The evening handoff before each trading day, plus each shift change, when the operator going off fills the Return section.

stall_points.description: Positions are corrected after the handoff email has gone out, so the shift has to merge several emails to know the real position.
stall_points.quote: We have also bought HE 21 and HE 22 from the APX.

stall_points.description: Other desks' positions sit in separate sheets, and the shift has to copy them across by hand. This invites missed or doubled entries.
stall_points.quote: ST-CALI is providing us with a sheet detailing their positions for RT, we will now be providing them with a sheet each morning detailing their sales from the previous day.

stall_points.description: Problems from the shift come back with no fixed place to record them, so mistakes surface as charges weeks later.
stall_points.quote: Send me an email each time the dispatchers remove requests on our behalf, or if We/PAC are/is unable to take the request out of their computer system.

stall_points.description: Enpower entry is split between the lead, deal entry and the shift. Open items wait until someone arrives or a price is filled in.
stall_points.quote: Kate has made the enpower for this deal (#672781, and #672785).  Please put the price in for deal #672781 (buy from EPE).

stall_points.description: Deal entry is pushed to the next morning, so the shift handles the schedule before the deals exist in Enpower.
stall_points.quote: I will do enpower for these deals when I arrive in the morning.

stall_points.description: Standing operating instructions are corrected by broadcast email. Nothing records which version is current.
stall_points.quote: After discussion with Roger, the Four Corners Units 4 and 5 are NOT take or pay.

stays_manual: Deciding positions, prices and which book carries them stays with the desk lead. That is a trading judgement.
Real-time purchases and sales during the shift, and calls to dispatchers (EPE, BPA, NEVP, LADWP), stay with the operators.
Contesting charges such as take-or-pay transmission bills stays manual. The Return log only gives the evidence trail.
Changing operating rules (unit ramp order, take-or-pay status) needs a person to confirm them with the plant or counterparty before they go into the log.
success_metric: Number of correction or follow-up emails per handoff to DL-Portland Real Time Shift ('one more time' re-sends), and the share of dispatcher-removed transmission requests recorded in the Return section on the same day
summary: The Portland real-time desk lead emails the shift every evening, in free text, with the next day's length and shorts, the book to use (ST-WBOM, ST-CALI, St-SW), deals already keyed in Enpower, and one-off duties. Those emails get re-sent with corrections, and problems such as dispatcher-removed transmission requests come back only by ad hoc email. A fixed handoff template, kept as a tab on the Service Sheet and sent to DL-Portland Real Time Shift, puts every position and every return item in the same fields each time. The modelled value is small, about $52 a month ($624 a year) at $85/h. The bigger gain is fewer missed entries and fewer correction re-sends.
